title: Archive through May 12, 2004 - Anonymous (Friday, April 30, 2004 - 07:59 pm)
content: I was attacked and stabbed 40-60 times and knew I would die but would also live if they got me to a hospital in time. I flat-lined, but cannot remember anything when I first arrived at the hospital. I then later flat-lined whilst in surgery in the intensive care dept. I think it was, it was then that I felt myself floating towards the ceiling. The horrendous pain I had been in was gone and it’s hard to describe but I felt surrounded/infused with this powerful "LOVE." It must be how a baby must feel whilst growing in its mother’s womb. I don't know how else to describe it. I felt safe. I remember looking down and seeing my body lying there with the doctors/nurses working on me, I could hear them saying she's not responding. One of the doctors told a nurse to stand clear. I remember looking at what they were wearing on their feet, and watching what they were doing and saying. It was then that I suddenly knew I had to go back, that there is a reason for me being alive today something I have yet to do. I then heard the doctor say stand clear we will try one last time - they had been trying to resuscitate me with those electric pad things. It was then that I felt a painfully sharp pain in my chest. It felt like I had been "sucked" back into my body, and I mean literally sucked. Apparently I was moved to the high dependency unit of intensive care where they say only one in ten go out alive. I was in a coma, but came out of it within 3 days. Although the doctors expected me to be in hospital for months, it was in fact only 3-4 weeks. Even though both my lungs had been stabbed 3-4 times each and had collapsed, both my kidneys had been lacerated several times, also my kidney, bowels and two main arteries had been severed, plus all the other stab wounds and the fact that I had lost so much blood that I should not have survived. To this day, the doctors, specialists, surgeons all say it was a miracle and that I should be dead. I recovered quickly and was walking out of the hospital within four weeks. Although I have been left with scars and no feeling in most parts of my body, left asthmatic and prone to infections, I know now I'm here for a purpose. I even know when things are going to happen, sometimes both good and bad like a women’s intuition but highly intensified. But that’s another thing that I could tell you about for ages. I'm still coming to terms with it as it sometimes creeps both myself and others out. Yet I know this has something to do with my N. D. E. Thank you for letting me tell someone this. Most people either don't want to hear about it 'cause it freaks them, or they look at me like I'm crazy. But no matter what, no-one will ever change my mind about what I experienced.

diagnosis.diagnosis_raw: Attacked and stabbed 40-60 times; both lungs stabbed multiple times and collapsed; kidneys lacerated; kidney, bowels and two main arteries severed; massive blood loss; coma.
diagnosis.disease_name: Severe penetrating trauma with cardiopulmonary arrest (flat-lined) and multi-organ injury
diagnosis.severity_description: Near-fatal multi-organ trauma with repeated cardiac arrest, collapsed lungs, severed arteries, massive blood loss, coma; ICU/high dependency unit
diagnosis.prognosis_given: Doctors expected months in hospital; told survival unlikely ("only one in ten go out alive"); told she should be dead
diagnosis.quality_of_life_impact: Coma; expected prolonged hospitalization; later residual numbness, scars, asthma, prone to infections
diagnosis.mobility_status: Coma; later recovered and walking out within ~4 weeks
diagnosis.vascular_condition: Two main arteries severed; massive blood loss; cardiac arrest requiring defibrillation

treatment.treatments_raw: Emergency surgery in intensive care; resuscitation attempts with electric pads (defibrillation); ICU/high dependency care; coma care
treatment.surgery_type: Surgery for multiple stab wounds/multi-organ injury (details not specified)
treatment.surgery_outcome: Survived and recovered rapidly (specific surgical outcomes not detailed)

remission_outcome.time_to_remission_raw: Came out of coma within 3 days; discharged walking within about 4 weeks (expected months)
remission_outcome.verification_detail: Physicians/specialists/surgeons reportedly said it was a "miracle" and she "should be dead"; clinical course described (coma 3 days; discharged in 3–4 weeks).
remission_outcome.physician_quote: “it was a miracle” / “I should be dead” (as reported by patient)

intuition_examples: Knew she would die but would also live if they got her to a hospital in time
During the experience, suddenly knew she had to go back because there was a reason/purpose for being alive
Reports ongoing intensified intuition/precognition about events
turner_factors.intuition_details: Describes strong inner knowing during the event and afterwards ("women’s intuition but highly intensified").
purpose_sources: Belief she is alive for a reason/purpose; something she has yet to do
turner_factors.purpose_details: States she knows she is here for a purpose and that this was realized during the NDE.

existential_shift.identity_shift_description: Reports being infused/surrounded by powerful love and feeling safe; afterward frames life as purpose-driven.
existential_shift.transformation_narrative: During the NDE she experienced relief from pain and an overwhelming sense of love/safety, then a strong knowing she must return because she has a reason to live; afterward she identifies a life purpose and reports heightened intuition.
existential_shift.pivot_point_description: While out of body observing resuscitation, she suddenly knew she had to go back because there was a reason she was alive.
existential_shift.transformation_timing: Occurred during cardiac arrest in surgery, before regaining consciousness and rapid physical recovery.

anomalous_experience.experience_description: During cardiac arrest in surgery, felt floating to the ceiling, pain ceased, surrounded by powerful love; saw her body and staff below; heard comments about not responding and "stand clear"; then felt sucked back into body with sharp chest pain.
anomalous_experience.experience_timing: During surgery in intensive care when she flat-lined (after initial arrival where she cannot remember).

validation.statistical_improbability_notes: Narrative describes repeated cardiac arrest, massive blood loss, collapsed lungs, severed arteries, and survival described by clinicians as highly unlikely ("one in ten").
validation.extraction_notes: This is a near-death/trauma survival narrative rather than a disease remission; verification relies on self-report without records, named clinicians, or imaging/lab specifics.

analysis.case_summary: After being stabbed 40–60 times with multi-organ injuries and repeated cardiac arrest during surgery, the patient reported an out-of-body near-death experience characterized by pain cessation and overwhelming love, then rapid recovery (coma resolved in 3 days; discharged walking in ~4 weeks) despite clinicians stating survival was unlikely.
key_healing_factors: Near-death experience with profound sense of love/safety and a felt mandate to return
Strong perceived life purpose after the event
Reported heightened intuition/precognition following the event
unique_features: Out-of-body perception during resuscitation with reported auditory/visual details (staff statements/actions)
Rapid recovery after extreme penetrating trauma and cardiac arrest described as a "miracle" by clinicians (per patient report)
analysis.analysis_notes: No cancer/autoimmune/infectious condition is described; the primary medical event is acute trauma with cardiac arrest and surgical resuscitation. Long-term outcomes include scars, numbness, asthma, and infections; no objective follow-up testing is provided.
